patch_description: Builds on the strongest prior program (Gen with 0.57): the adaptive quadratic endpoint fit plus zero-lag bidirectional one-pole smoothing, which already reduced slope changes to ~100 and false reversals to ~77. Per the recommendation, the noisy per-sample reversal-damping loop (which can distort genuine dynamics) is replaced by a single lightweight local mechanism: a deadband applied directly to the fused bidirectional-filtered velocity. The fused velocity is computed from forward- and backward-pass state differences (vel_f, vel_b), combined, then shrunk toward zero by a noise-adaptive threshold (~0.2 × std of the input's first differences). Where the deadband zeroes the velocity, the level is corrected to stay on the prior value, eliminating spurious micro-reversals without an extra pipeline stage, while genuine large slope changes pass through untouched so lag error and responsiveness remain intact.
